ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: Deep Diving
ModMetaData.author: mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
SEA_DIVE_MAPS_BUILD_1 (question card 2026-09-25: dive opens a small dedicated underwater pocket map — not "surface in shallows," not "decide later"). Retires this mod's original v1 content, SCALD_DIVING_MOD_1's shore "dive to hunt/commune" terrain-standing interaction, per the owner's SHIP-ONLY ACCESS ruling (2026-09-26, verbatim, mid-turn): "the gravship is the sole dive/resurface mechanism... don't let the players walk from tile to tile on the worldmap... remove any dive options from shore." That shore mechanism (RM_DiveEligible tag, its float-menu provider, both JobDrivers) is gone from this mod entirely — a sea tile stays worldmap-impassable, and the only way down is a ship.
**The generic mechanism (this mod's actual surface, RM-tier because it names no sea, no clan, no planet):** `RM_SeaDiveHatch` is a buildable `MapPortal` — right-click "Enter" to descend to a real pocket map generated fresh each time, using whichever sea biome the parent map's tile currently carries. One ThingDef, one C# class (`RM_SeaDiveHatch`); the pocket-map generator is chosen at generate time from `Map.Biome`, not baked into four separate hatch defs. A `PocketMapExit`-derived ascent line (`RM_SeaDiveExit`) returns colonists to the ship automatically — vanilla's own `PocketMapExit.SpawnSetup` links it back to whichever hatch generated the map, no bespoke plumbing needed.
**Why the pocket map has to seed its own cast:** MEASURED live 2026-09-26 (this item's ledger) — a sea BiomeDef's wildAnimals list never spawns at a standable cell on a re-tiled sea tile, because the vanilla spawn chooser reads the map's per-cell blended biome and a sea's only cells are its own unstandable water. `GenStep_SeaFloorFauna` (one class, reused by all four sea generators, parameterized purely by `map.Biome`) explicitly spawns each sea's own wildAnimals rows onto its pocket map instead of trusting ambient spawning to do it.
**Ship-only, enforced at construction, not at use:** `RM_SeaDiveHatch` can only be built on a map that already carries a real, existing ThingDef — `GravEngine` (Odyssey) — via `PlaceWorker_NeedsGravEngine`. This is a concrete, checkable-offline stand-in for "somewhere inside a gravship"; it does not model or assume anything about whether a gravship can legally travel to or land at an impassable sea tile in the first place — that is a separate, open engine question for a future item, not settled here.
**Deliberately NOT in this build** (see SEA_DIVE_MAPS_BUILD_1's close report for the full list): the weighted-belt apparel item itself, the two-axis (no-air / temperature) dive-gear matrix, per-sea floor dressing (chimney-iron ore, floor droids, the Scald's Rakatan wreck, named bottom-walker fauna), and heat-gated hazard zones. The mechanism this mod now ships is the map-generation and floor-cast half only — every named species already on each sea's own BiomeDef will spawn once its hatch is built and entered; nothing about its ART or LOOT is new here.
**Mod Settings** (MOD_OPTIONS_RETROFIT_1 doctrine): master on/off (no hatch anywhere is enterable when off), and a "require a grav engine" toggle (shipped default ON, matching the ruling above; off exists only for testing or a different ruleset, never the shipped experience).
